chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was taken on the Night Journey and reached al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, the time of salat came. Jibra'il عليه السلام gave the adhan and the iqamah, then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stepped forward, and the angels and the prophets formed rows behind the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. He said: We asked him, 'How did he give the adhan?' He said: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. I testify that there is no god but Allah, I testify that there is no god but Allah. I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Hayya 'ala al-salat, hayya 'ala al-salat. Hayya 'ala al-falah, hayya 'ala al-falah. Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal, hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah.' And the iqamah is like it, except that in it there is 'Qad qamat al-salat, qad qamat al-salat' between 'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal, hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal' and 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.' So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed Bilal to use it, and he continued to call the adhan with it until the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed away.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, and Kulayb al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

He recounted to them the adhan and the iqamah, and said: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. I testify that there is no god but Allah, I testify that there is no god but Allah. I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Hayya 'ala al-salat, hayya 'ala al-salat. Hayya 'ala al-falah, hayya 'ala al-falah. Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal, hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah.' And the iqamah is likewise.

key_terms.أَذَّنَ: gave the adhan, the call announcing the time of salat
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: the iqamah, the call immediately preceding the commencement of salat
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ الْمَعْمُورَ: the frequented heavenly house reached during the Night Journey
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ: come to salat; an invitation to the prayer
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ: come to success; a call to spiritual success through worship
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: come to the best of deeds; a phrase included in the adhan here
key_terms.صَفَّ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالنَّبِيُّونَ: the angels and the prophets formed rows behind him in prayer
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the salat has been established; wording specific to the iqamah

ai.seo_question: What is the wording and number of phrases in the adhan and iqamah according to Shia hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the adhan and iqamah as taught in the heavenly ascent of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, where Jibra'il عليه السلام called them before the congregational salat of the prophets and angels. It also transmits a report from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام recounting their wording, emphasizing the established form of the adhan and iqamah, including 'ḥayya 'alā khayr al-'amal.'
